facts: Full year 2025 worldwide revenue was $90.5 million, an 8% increase over the prior year (7% on a constant currency basis).
Q4 2025 U.S. revenue was $14.1 million, an 11% decrease year-over-year, and full year 2025 U.S. revenue was $57 million, only a 1% increase over the prior year.
Approximately half of the U.S. sales organization turned over during 2025, driven by disrupted roles, suboptimal incentive structures, and competing initiatives.

The company executed a cost restructuring initiative reducing ongoing operating expenses by over 10%, with most reductions coming from G&A and marketing while preserving sales force and R&D investments.

The company closed a $60 million credit facility with a 5-year interest-only structure, including a $40 million initial term loan and an option to draw an incremental $20 million through end of 2027, extending debt maturity to 2031.
Annual cash burn is expected to decrease from $32 million in 2025 to $23 million in 2026, a reduction of nearly 30%, with cash and marketable securities of $69.8 million as of December 31, 2025.

Full year 2026 revenue guidance is $90 million to $92 million, with U.S. sales growth expected to resume in the back half of the year, progressing from mid-to-high single-digit declines in Q1 to high single-digit growth in Q4.

Full year 2026 operating expenses are expected to be $113 million to $115 million (including ~$21 million noncash stock-based compensation), implying a 7% to 9% decrease excluding SBC from 2025 levels.
AeriSeal CONVERT II pivotal trial enrollment is expected to be completed in 2027, with the potential to grow the total addressable market by an estimated 20% globally.

China sales were less than 5% of global revenue in 2025, with renewal of the Chinese registration certificate expected in the second half of 2026, creating a timing mismatch that will depress international year-over-year growth in H1 2026 before flipping to double-digit growth in H2.
IFF's net debt to credit adjusted EBITDA improved from 3.8x at the end of 2024 to 2.6x at the end of 2025, with gross debt decreasing by nearly $3 billion to approximately $6 billion.

Full year 2026 guidance calls for sales of $10.5 billion to $10.8 billion (1% to 4% comparable currency-neutral growth) and EBITDA of $2.05 billion to $2.15 billion (3% to 8% comparable currency-neutral growth).
Full year 2025 free cash flow was $256 million, including approximately $300 million of Reg G-related charges primarily driven by divestiture activities and a $166 million working capital outflow.
IFF formally launched the sale process for its Food Ingredients business approximately two weeks prior to the call, with strong interest from both strategic buyers and financial sponsors.

Health & Biosciences delivered Q4 EBITDA of $155 million, a 20% year-over-year increase, while the health sub-segment remained down low single digits and is expected to return to growth in the second half of 2026.

The company invested approximately $100 million in 2025 into innovation capabilities in high-growth, high-margin categories, with benefits expected to materialize in the second half of 2026 and more fully in 2027.
Incremental margins on volume growth are approximately 30% to 35% depending on the business segment, and 2026 growth is expected to be primarily volume-driven with pricing slightly down.

The Taste segment delivered Q4 EBITDA of $94 million, a 17% increase year-over-year, driven by high single-digit sales growth in North America from new wins, favorable net pricing, and cost discipline.

IFF returned $409 million to shareholders through dividends and $38 million through share repurchases in 2025, with a minimum annual share buyback target of $80 million to $100 million to offset dilution.

Q1 2026 is expected to show muted sales and only modest EBITDA growth versus a like-for-like Q1 2025 base of approximately $505 million (adjusted for divestitures), with year-over-year growth expected to progressively improve each quarter.
Q3 FY2026 net sales reached $1.2 billion, up 2% (~$19 million) year-over-year, with adjusted EPS of $5.31, a 4% increase versus the prior year.

Acuity Brands Lighting (ABL) sales declined 2% to $905 million against a tough prior-year comparison (pre-tariff order pull-forward), and adjusted operating margin contracted 60 bps to 18.2%, though gross margin remained strong at 46.1%.
Acuity Intelligence Spaces (AIS) sales grew 15% to $304 million with adjusted operating profit up 22.5% to $76 million and operating margin expanding 150 bps to 25.1%, driven by Distech and QSC.
Management said lighting demand is 'firming' after softness from October through January, and Q4 should show sequential growth from Q3, though likely less steep than the Q3 step-up.
On a 2-year stacked basis, total ABL grew 1% and the combined independent/direct sales networks grew 4%, normalizing for tariff-driven order timing.
Year-to-date operating cash flow reached $520 million, $121 million higher than the prior-year period, supporting aggressive capital returns.
The company repaid $200 million of term loan, raised the dividend 18%, and repurchased over 766,000 shares for $230 million YTD, including ~500,000 shares this quarter at an average price of $281.
Acuity refinanced into a new 5-year $800 million unsecured revolving credit facility, upsizing capacity and extending maturities.
Distech is expanding into the data center vertical via the new Eclipse Resilience PLC controller, complementing its DDC platform and positioning the company to supply multiple hyperscalers.

Management flagged inflation pressures (metals, ~12% medical cost increase, memory chip supply shocks primarily affecting AIS) but expects continued ABL gross margin expansion through product vitality, productivity, and pricing even in a soft volume environment.
Air Products delivered fiscal year 2025 earnings per share of $12.03, above the midpoint of full year guidance, with operating income margin of 23.7% and return on capital of 10.1%.
The company returned $1.6 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2025, marking its 43rd consecutive year of dividend increases.
For fiscal year 2026, Air Products expects earnings per share in the range of $12.85 to $13.15, representing 7% to 9% growth from the prior year.
Since 2022, the company has identified 3,600 headcount reductions (16% of peak workforce), expected to contribute approximately $250 million in annual cost savings or $0.90 per share once complete.
Capital expenditures are expected to be approximately $4 billion in fiscal 2026, declining to roughly $2.5 billion per year after large projects are completed.
The NEOM project is approximately 90% complete, with solar and wind power generation expected by early 2026 and full ammonia production availability in 2027.
Air Products has approximately $2.5 billion remaining to spend on underperforming projects from 2026 to 2028, which are not expected to contribute materially to operating income.

The company is evaluating proposals to divest carbon sequestration and ammonia production assets from its Louisiana blue hydrogen project and has halted new commitments until an offtake agreement is reached.
Helium headwinds are expected to continue in fiscal 2026 at approximately 4%, comparable to fiscal 2025 levels.
The company expects to be modestly cash flow positive in fiscal 2026 and is committed to staying cash flow neutral through 2028 as it closes out several projects.
PBF reported Q1 2026 adjusted net loss of $0.88 per share and adjusted EBITDA of $68.7 million, with results hurt by West Coast operations, higher RINs expense, and derivative losses.

The Martinez refinery's cat feed hydrotreater and alkylation unit are operating, with the FCC expected to produce finished products this weekend, completing the phased restart that was delayed beyond the rebuild's February completion.
PBF recognized over $200 million in aggregate derivative losses during Q1, with approximately $100 million unrealized expected to be mostly offset in Q2 as physical barrels are processed.
The company received a $106.5 million gain on insurance recoveries in Q1, bringing cumulative Martinez fire insurance recoveries to $1 billion net of deductibles, with additional payments expected.

Q1 cash used in operations was $324 million, including a working capital draw of roughly $340 million driven by inventory build (approximately 6 million barrels above normal) ahead of Martinez restart.
PBF ended Q1 with $542 million cash, approximately $2.3 billion net debt, net debt-to-cap of 36%, and roughly $2.4 billion of liquidity.

Consolidated Q1 CapEx was $320 million (excluding $189 million of Martinez incident-related capital) and included approximately $100 million of net 2025 carryover that hadn't been cash-settled at year-end.

The Refining Business Improvement program achieved its 2025 target of $230 million in annualized run-rate savings (including ~$160 million of OpEx reductions vs. 2024), with management on track toward the $350 million year-end 2026 goal.
Management indicated the Martinez hydrocracker turnaround originally planned for Q2 will likely be pushed to late Q3, leaving a clean runway across Q2 and Q3 to capture strong margins.

SBR produced an average of 16,700 barrels per day of renewable diesel in Q1, contributed approximately $8 million of EBITDA to PBF, and management expects significantly stronger results following the RVO finalization and a recent catalyst change.
Q3 2025 consolidated sales were $485 million, down 12% or $69 million from Q3 2024.
Q3 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $70.9 million with a 14.6% margin, compared to $77.4 million in Q3 2024.
Adjusted EPS for Q3 2025 was $1.21 per share compared to $1.37 in the prior year quarter.
Year-to-date adjusted SG&A was down 14% compared to prior year, equating to over $19 million in savings.
The company revised 2025 consolidated sales guidance to $1.9 billion, down from $2.1 billion in 2024.
2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance was revised to $255 million to $260 million, compared to $262 million in 2024.
2025 adjusted EPS guidance was set at $4.00 to $4.15 per share.
Net debt at September 30 was $885 million, approximately $45 million lower than June 30, with a net leverage ratio of 3.4x.
The Catalyst initiative is expected to deliver approximately $80 million of ongoing benefits by the end of 2028, with over $40 million captured in 2025.
2025 capital expenditures are projected at $52 million to $55 million, a significant reduction from $74 million in 2024.
Q3 2026 adjusted EBITDA increased 6.6% to $410.6 million, above the high end of guidance, while net income fell 28.5% year-over-year to $41.7 million and adjusted diluted EPS rose just 1.3% to $0.80.
Total net sales grew 6.4% with total company cases up 4.4%, driven by 6.5% organic independent restaurant case growth (exceeding the 6% benchmark) and 8.3% organic convenience case growth.

The Convenience segment delivered standout 34.1% adjusted EBITDA growth and 8.7% total revenue growth, with Love's and RaceTrac onboarding accounting for the majority of segment growth and expected to provide incremental benefit through mid-fiscal 2027.
PFG tightened full-year 2026 guidance to sales of $67.7B–$68.0B (from $67.25B–$68.25B) and adjusted EBITDA of $1.90B–$1.93B (from $1.875B–$1.975B), implying a midpoint trim to Q4.

The Specialty segment posted negative EBITDA year-over-year despite 5.3% revenue growth, hurt by lapping prior-year inventory gains and elevated shipping and fuel costs, with case growth of only 1.1%.

Cheney Brothers continues to drag fiscal 2026 results due to higher-than-expected expenses tied to the new Florence, SC distribution facility, with spillover into Q4 as the fourth and final customer transition wave was delayed by weather.
Gross profit per case rose $0.20 year-over-year, with foodservice inflation at 1.5%, specialty at 5.1%, convenience at 7.9%, and total company cost inflation at approximately 4.5%.

PFG generated over $1 billion of operating cash flow and $806 million of free cash flow in the first nine months of 2026, up $312 million year-over-year, with CapEx of approximately $266 million tracking below the 70 bps of revenue long-term target.
The company closed a late-Q3 acquisition of Cash-Wa, a broadline foodservice distributor with three facilities covering Nebraska and the Dakotas, expanding PFG's western footprint.

Independent net new account growth was approximately 5.4% with a 100 bps differential to total case growth indicating positive penetration; brand penetration to independents hit a record 54% in legacy Foodservice while Cheney sits at 15%–20%, blending to roughly 50%.
Q3 2025 GAAP net income was $21.5 million with EPS of $0.73 per share, while non-GAAP core net income was $21.2 million with core EPS of $0.72.
Core ROAA was 1.06% for Q3 2025, with management targeting a roughly 1.2% core ROAA run rate by end of Q4 2025.
Core efficiency ratio improved to 60.45% for the quarter, reflecting three consecutive quarters of essentially flat core noninterest expenses.
The correspondent banking unit is expected to generate over $17 million in revenue this year, contributing roughly $5 million to net income.
Total loans held for investment declined $26.6 million (1.7% annualized) as paydowns of $479 million exceeded new loan production of $452 million.
Total deposits increased $87.2 million, with interest-bearing deposits up $131.4 million offset by noninterest-bearing deposits declining $44.15 million.
GAAP net interest margin remained unchanged at 3.68%, while core net interest margin declined 1 basis point to 3.63%.

The company has approximately $3 billion in floating rate loans at 7.33% weighted average rate and $646 million in fixed rate loans maturing over the next 12 months at 6.30% expected to reprice in the mid-to-low 7% range.
Progressive Bank acquisition is expected to close early Q1 2026 with system conversion scheduled for August 2026.
The quarterly common stock dividend was increased by $0.01, marking the ninth consecutive year of dividend increases.
Q3 organic net sales grew 2.4% to approximately $2.8 billion, returning to growth with volumes up 0.5% and price/mix up 1.9%.
Adjusted EPS fell to $0.39 from $0.51 a year ago, a $0.12 decline driven by inflation exceeding productivity, lower Ardent Mills equity earnings, and reduced profit from divested businesses.
Full-year adjusted EPS guidance was set to approximately $1.70, the low end of the $1.70-$1.85 range, entirely due to a $0.10 headwind from the Ardent Mills JV rather than core business weakness.
Free cash flow conversion estimate was raised again to approximately 105%, up from 100% at CAGNY and 90% at the start of the year.
Net debt was reduced by over $800 million year-over-year (about $300 million in Q3 alone), exceeding the prior $700 million target, with net leverage at 3.83x versus a long-term goal of 3x.
Refrigerated & Frozen delivered organic net sales growth of 3.6% on nearly 4% volume growth, with 88% of the frozen portfolio holding or gaining volume share.
Snacks dollar sales outpaced category growth for the fifth consecutive quarter, with meat snacks up roughly 9% in dollars and 10% in volume.
Adjusted operating margin declined 213 basis points to 10.6%, though full-year margin is now guided near the high end of the 11%-11.5% range.
Total inflation remained elevated at roughly 7% including tariffs, offset partially by core productivity of over 5% of cost of goods sold.

Adjusted equity earnings guidance was lowered to approximately $140 million due to Ardent Mills, reflecting lower wheat prices and volatility, and no share repurchases or M&A occurred in the quarter while the $1.40 annual dividend was maintained.
Cash and cash equivalents stood at approximately $56 million as of March 20, 2026, with 74 million common shares outstanding.

The company completed an oversubscribed equity offering earlier in 2026, raising approximately $57.5 million in gross proceeds ($53 million net of expenses), driven by leading institutional investors including Hood River, Gratia, and MA Capital.

Comstock Metals generated approximately $1.4 million in reported revenue for 2025 (up from $0.4 million in 2024), plus an additional $2.2 million in deferred revenue billings, totaling approximately $3.5 million for the year as guided.

The first industry-scale metals recycling facility is on schedule for commissioning in Q1 and operations in Q2 2026, with substantially all equipment received and ovens arriving imminently via approximately 20 full 18-wheeler truckloads.

Management projects 2026 revenue ramping from $100,000-$200,000 per month to $1-2 million per month, with a $2 million monthly run rate ($24-25 million annualized) expected to be remarkably profitable.

Each recycling facility costs $12-16 million to build but can generate $75-80 million in annual cash flow when running at full capacity, processing approximately 3.3 million panels per year per production line.

The company's ownership in Sierra Springs Opportunity Fund (SSOF) has increased from just under 17% to over 36-37% and could exceed 50%, with estimated asset values in the hundreds of millions driven by Northern Nevada data center demand.
Mining asset monetization discussions are underway with serious, capitalized counterparties at a potential value range of $50-60 million, with an expected 75-90 day timeline to close.

The company identified a second recycling facility site in Clark County (outside Las Vegas), has already submitted permits, and plans to order equipment soon with a target of commissioning by Q4 2026 or Q1 2027.

At current silver prices of approximately $70 per ounce, the company's offtake revenue per ton of tailings increases from a modeled $125 to $375, with two Nevada facilities projected to produce approximately 2.5 million ounces of silver annually from recycled panels.
Subscription revenue grew 27% year-over-year to $141 million in Q3 2025.
International revenue grew 37% year-over-year, representing 34% of total revenue.
Billings increased 20% year-over-year to $178 million, including roughly $4 million of accelerated billings from Q4 due to early renewals and add-ons.
AI bookings were up 60% year-over-year for the first nine months of 2025.
Total RPO grew 24% year-over-year to $1.2 billion, with 12-month cRPO up 29% year-over-year.
Non-GAAP operating income increased 69% year-over-year to $9.3 million, representing 6% of revenue.
License revenue declined 64% year-over-year to $4 million due to contract rationalization and SaaS conversions in the federal business.
Full year 2025 revenue guidance was raised to $594-596 million with non-GAAP operating margin expected between 2-3%.
Management stated they are comfortable with current Wall Street consensus for full year 2026 revenue and non-GAAP operating income.
One customer reported SensibleAI Forecast reduced forecast generation time by 94%, freeing up more than 13,000 labor hours annually.
Q3 2025 marked Playboy's first quarter of positive net income ($0.5 million) since going public, representing the third consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA at $4.1 million.
Licensing revenue increased 61% year-over-year in Q3, with 6 new licensing deals signed during the quarter and 14 total deals year-to-date.
Honey Birdette comparable store sales grew 22% year-over-year while gross margins expanded 700 basis points from 54% to 61%.
Playboy was awarded $81 million in damages through a Hong Kong arbitration against a former Chinese licensee and is pursuing enforcement in China.
The company ended Q3 with over $32 million in cash and extended its debt facility maturity to May 2028 with reduced interest rates upon prepayments.
Playboy signed a nonbinding term sheet with Miami investors for a $25 million investment into Playboy Hospitality to fund a Playboy club in Miami Beach.
The Great Playmate Search attracted approximately 16,000 contestants representing a combined social media following of more than 200 million, generating over 1 million votes from over 100,000 users.
Adjusted EBITDA included $2.5 million in litigation expenses; excluding those expenses, adjusted EBITDA would have been $6.6 million.
Honey Birdette's average order value increased 9% since the website relaunch, and full-price items increased by 15%.
Management expects paid voting to become a multimillion-dollar annual business, with plans to run 4 to 10 different contests per year starting in 2026.
Q3 2025 consolidated revenue was $18.8 million, a 36.9% year-over-year increase from $13.7 million in Q3 2024.
The OSS segment achieved revenue growth of 43.4% year-over-year in Q3 2025.
On a trailing 12-month basis, the OSS segment had a book-to-bill ratio of 1.4.
The company raised its full year 2025 consolidated revenue guidance from $59-$61 million to $63-$65 million.
Q3 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $1.2 million compared to an adjusted EBITDA loss of $6 million in the prior year third quarter.
The company reported GAAP net income of $0.3 million or $0.01 per diluted share in Q3 2025 compared to a net loss of $6.8 million or $0.32 per share in Q3 2024.
OSS completed a registered direct offering on October 1, 2025, raising approximately $12.5 million in gross proceeds.
The P-8 Poseidon Reconnaissance aircraft platform has generated lifetime contracted revenue exceeding $50 million to date.
A medical imaging OEM relationship has a 5-year expected program value of over $25 million.
OSS segment gross margin improved to 45.6% in Q3 2025 compared to an adjusted gross margin of 43.2% in Q3 2024.
Kymera ended Q3 2025 with a cash balance of $978.7 million, providing runway into the second half of 2028.
Q3 2025 revenue was $2.8 million, entirely from the Gilead collaboration.
R&D expenses for Q3 2025 were $74.1 million, with adjusted cash R&D spend of $65.7 million reflecting a 7% decrease from Q2 2025.
The Phase IIb BROADEN2 study in atopic dermatitis will enroll approximately 200 patients across 3 doses plus placebo over a 16-week treatment period, with top line results expected by mid-2027.
The BREADTH Phase IIb asthma trial is on track to initiate in Q1 2026.
Phase Ib BroADen study in atopic dermatitis is fully enrolled with dosing complete, and results will be reported in December 2025.
KT-579 (IRF5 degrader) has completed IND-enabling studies and will advance into a Phase I healthy volunteer study early in 2026 with data expected in 2026.
Kymera is eligible to receive a total of $85 million in upfront and option payments from Gilead, with approximately half already received as the upfront payment.
Sanofi is expected to advance KT-485 (IRAK4 program) into Phase I testing in 2026, which would trigger a development milestone payable to Kymera.

In published dupilumab studies where baseline TARC levels were higher than healthy volunteers, TARC reduction was in the range of 70% to 80% at 4 weeks, which is the benchmark Kymera has set for KT-621.
Q3 2025 revenue was $218.2 million, slightly ahead of the midpoint of guidance, with gross margin of 54% including approximately a 1 percentage point impact from tariffs.
Q4 2025 revenue guidance is $250 million to $265 million, representing 15% to 21% sequential growth, with revenue from 2.5D packaging customers expected to nearly double from Q3.
Advanced nodes revenue is expected to double to approximately $300 million for full year 2025 compared to $148.5 million in full year 2024.
Specialty devices and advanced packaging revenue is expected to finish slightly higher than $500 million for the full year 2025.
Q3 cash from operations increased sequentially to $83 million from $58 million in Q2, representing approximately 185% cash conversion of non-GAAP net income.
The company successfully shipped over 30% of Q3 tools from extended factories in Asia and expects to be capable of shipping over 60% of production from international locations by end of Q1 2026.
The Semilab acquisition will involve $432.3 million in cash and 641,771 shares, with total transaction value of approximately $495 million, about $50 million less than original terms.
3Di technology completed full qualification at 2 high-bandwidth memory customers in the quarter, with discussions started for volume orders to support next-generation HBM devices.
Packaging customers are indicating potential need for as much as 20% more tools to support expansions and new applications for 2D subsurface and 3Di inspection technologies.
Q4 2025 EPS guidance is $1.18 to $1.33 per share, with operating margins expected to rebound to 24% to 26% on operating expenses of approximately $77 million.
Average daily production increased 27% year-over-year in Q4 2025 to 35,100 BOE per day, with full year 2025 production averaging 32,000 BOE per day (28% year-over-year growth).
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDAX was $315 million and total capital expenditures were $401 million, indicating an outspend of approximately $86 million.

The company's 2026 guidance projects production of 34,000 to 36,000 BOE per day (9% year-over-year growth) with development capital of $300 million to $330 million, roughly 15% less than 2025 spending.
Net debt to adjusted EBITDAX was 1.2x at year-end 2025, with $350 million outstanding on 2029 senior notes, $50 million drawn on the revolver, and total liquidity of $339.5 million.
The company expects to achieve free cash flow from operations in 2027 at current strip prices, with maintenance capital estimated at approximately $250 million.

In 2025, the company invested $122 million across 107 transactions, securing approximately 20,500 net acres and 77.2 net locations at an average Permian acquisition cost of $1.4 million per net location, well below recent public market transaction comps.

Q4 2025 average realized oil price was $55.49 per barrel (vs. $65.53 in Q4 2024) and natural gas averaged $1.81 per Mcf (48% of Henry Hub), with weak Waha pricing meaningfully impacting revenue and EBITDAX.

The company partnered with Conduit Power to support 200 megawatts of natural gas-fired power generation in ERCOT (expected fully online in 2027), expected to enhance Permian gas realizations by approximately $1 to $2 per Mcf.
Oil exit-to-exit production growth from Q4 2025 to Q4 2026 is expected to be 12%, with oil volumes forecast at approximately 51% of total 2026 production.
Approximately 90% of capital invested in 2026 will be focused on operated projects, with planned net wells declining from 38 in 2025 to approximately 29 in 2026.
Q4 2025 revenue reached a record $172.6 million, representing 23% year-over-year growth and exceeding the high end of guidance range of $159 million to $163 million.
Q4 gross margin hit a record high of 64%, up 650 basis points from 57.5% in Q4 2024, with incremental gross margin on a trailing basis reaching 76%.
Security revenue grew 32% year-over-year to $35.4 million in Q4, comprising 21% of total revenue, while network services revenue grew 19% to $130.8 million.
RPO reached a record $353.8 million, growing 55% year-over-year, with the current portion representing 70% of total RPO and growing 37% year-over-year.

Full year 2025 free cash flow was positive $45.8 million compared to negative $35.7 million in 2024, an $81.6 million improvement and materially above the original guidance midpoint of negative $15 million.
Trailing 12-month net retention rate improved to 110%, up from 106% in the prior quarter and 102% in the year-ago quarter.

For 2026, the company guided revenue of $700 million to $720 million (14% growth at midpoint) and non-GAAP operating profit of $50 million to $60 million, representing a doubling in operating margin to 8% versus 4% in 2025.
Price erosion contracted to mid-single digits in Q4 from historical mid-teens levels, reflecting improved pricing discipline and focus on performance-driven customer segments.

Infrastructure capital expenditures are expected to increase to 10%-12% of 2026 revenue from 5% in 2025, driven partly by memory component price increases of 25%-75% and capacity expansion including new POPs in APJ.

The company raised $180 million in 0% convertible notes due 2030 with a 32.5% conversion premium and executed capped call transactions totaling $18 million representing a 100% conversion premium at $23.04 per share.
Q1 2026 total revenues were $424 million, growing 14.5% year-over-year and 11.9% in constant currency, with subscription revenues (93% of total) up 14.7% (12.2% constant currency).
Year-over-year ARR growth in Q1 was 11.5% constant currency, ending the quarter at $1.495 billion, with sequential quarterly growth of 2.5%, all organic.
Net revenue retention rate remained at 109% and account retention at 99%, with new logos contributing 300 basis points of ARR growth, primarily within SMB.
AOI less operating SBC (the new primary profitability metric) was $141 million in Q1 with a 33.2% margin, with operating expenses weighted more toward the first half of 2026.
Q1 free cash flow was $188 million, with LTM free cash flow of $492 million up 13%, and management reaffirmed the full year 2026 free cash flow outlook of $500 million to $570 million.

The company repaid $678 million of 2026 convertible notes at maturity, reducing fully diluted share count by ~10.6 million (3%), and closed a new $550 million term loan A bringing total credit facility capacity to $1.85 billion; net debt leverage fell from 2.1x to 1.9x.
Capital returned to shareholders in Q1 included $54 million in share repurchases and $21 million in dividends.
Bentley Asset Analytics, spawned by AI, has surpassed $50 million in annual revenue run rate, and a new GM (Bryan Friehauf, formerly GE Vernova/Hitachi) has been appointed to scale it.

45% of revenue comes from 220 accounts spending over $1 million annually, and ~2/3 of revenue from 824 accounts spending over $250,000; top design firms account for ~$414 million ARR (~28% of total), with 470 of 614 ex-China top global firms as customers.

Resources is now the fastest-growing sector and second largest at over 20% of sector-attributable ARR, with subsurface ARR in civil infrastructure up 4x since the Seequent acquisition; China represents ~2% of ARR, and perpetual license revenues fell 18% in constant currency while services grew 25.8%.
McDonald's delivered system-wide sales of nearly $140 billion in 2025, up 5.5% in constant currency for the full year, with full-year comp sales growth of more than 3% and over 5.5% in Q4.
In Q4, U.S. comp sales were up 6.8%, driven by positive check and guest count growth, and the U.S. achieved its strongest comp guest count gap to near-end competitors in recent history.

McDonald's opened 2,275 gross restaurants in 2025 and is targeting approximately 2,600 gross openings in 2026 (with about 2,100 net additions representing ~4.5% unit growth), on track to reach 50,000 restaurants by end of 2027.
Full-year adjusted operating margin was 46.9%, with total restaurant margin dollars exceeding $15 billion; the company expects operating margin to expand into the mid- to high 40% range in 2026.

The loyalty program now has nearly 210 million 90-day active users across 70 markets, up from about $20 billion in loyalty system-wide sales in 2023 to nearly double that in 2025, with a target of 250 million active users by end of 2027.
In the U.S., average customer visit frequency increased from 10.5 times per year before joining the loyalty program to 26 times per year after becoming a loyalty member, a more than 2.5x increase.
Capital expenditures were $3.4 billion in 2025 and are expected to increase to $3.7 billion to $3.9 billion in 2026, with the majority invested in new unit openings across U.S. and IOM segments.

The U.S. beverage test across more than 500 restaurants in Q4 exceeded expectations, driving incremental occasions across snack, dinner and evening dayparts as well as higher average check, with a broader McCafe-branded launch planned for later in 2026.

The company expects Q1 2026 U.S. comp sales growth to decelerate sequentially from Q4's 6.8%, with severe weather in late January estimated to create approximately 100 basis points of drag for the full quarter.

McDonald's expects foreign currency to be a tailwind of $0.20 to $0.30 to full-year 2026 EPS, interest expense to increase 4% to 6% year-over-year, and the effective tax rate to be between 21% and 23%.
TaskUs delivered Q4 2025 revenue of $313 million, representing 14.1% year-over-year growth and beating the top end of quarterly guidance by nearly $10 million.
Full year 2025 revenue was $1.184 billion (19% year-over-year growth) with adjusted EBITDA of $249.1 million at a 21% margin.

The company declared a $3.65 per share special dividend (approximately $333 million total) payable in March 2026, funded by a refinanced $500 million term loan at SOFR plus 2.75% maturing in March 2031.

Full year 2026 revenue guidance is $1.21 billion to $1.24 billion (approximately 3.5% growth at midpoint), with the deceleration from 2025 primarily driven by the largest client's plans to leverage AI for efficiencies.
AI Services was the fastest-growing service line with 45.9% year-over-year growth in Q4 (reaching $57.5 million) and nearly 59% for the full year, exceeding $200 million in annual revenue.

ORLADEYO retention remains consistent with historical trends at 60% of patients reaching one year, while management reiterated confidence in reaching $1 billion in peak ORLADEYO sales and identified a U.S. Netherton syndrome market opportunity of 3,000+ patients with BCX17725 proof-of-concept data expected by year-end 2026.
Atea maintained approximately $329.3 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities at the end of Q3 2025, providing runway through 2027.
The company expects to complete patient enrollment for the North American Phase III trial C-BEYOND next month, with top line results anticipated mid-2026.

Atea announced the conclusion of its formal engagement with Evercore, its strategic advisor, stating that positive Phase III outcomes would strengthen its ability to secure attractive terms.
Atea's HCV regimen offers 8 weeks of treatment for non-cirrhotic patients compared to 12 weeks with the standard of care (Epclusa).

Atea estimates the hepatitis E market opportunity could translate into roughly $500 million to $750 million per year or more, with potential for orphan drug designation.
Q1 2026 revenue was $34 million, down 6% year-over-year, with average paid members of 632,000, down 4% year-over-year.

The company expanded distribution via its Bring Your Own Card (BYOC) strategy, renewed referral partnerships with ANZ and Kiwibank, and added new integrations including Campfire, Rillet, and American Airlines.
Q1 2026 total revenue grew 13% year-over-year to $207 million, with adjusted EBITDA of $36 million at an 18% margin, both exceeding company expectations.

Partnerships (including LinkedIn, Chase, and a new exclusive deal with GoDaddy) drove 10% of total orders in Q1, up from 4% a year ago, while new ChatGPT and Claude integrations are not yet material to traffic.

AI is driving operational efficiencies including a 55% reduction in trademark classification search time, 30% faster patent drafting, ~40% of customer care chats resolved end-to-end by agentic AI, and a ~1/3 reduction in missed sales opportunities.

Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $810–$830 million (~8% growth at midpoint) with adjusted EBITDA reiterated at $190–$200 million (~13% growth); Q2 revenue is guided to $203–$207 million with adjusted EBITDA of $40–$42 million.

Advanced technology (dominated by data centers) rose to 56% of revenue, with the industrial sector at 75% of volume; modular accounted for 17% of revenue.
The company announced a definitive agreement to acquire an electrical contractor in the West, expected to close in early May, contributing ~$250 million annualized revenue at 8%-10% EBITDA margins.

Devon delivered Q1 2026 oil production of 387,000 barrels per day, reaching the top end of its guidance range, while capital spending came in 6% below the midpoint of guidance.
Q1 2026 free cash flow was $816 million, reflecting beats on both production and capital.

Devon will achieve its $1 billion business optimization target ahead of schedule, with contributions from capital efficiency, production optimization, commercial improvements, and corporate cost reductions.

Both Devon and Coterra paused share repurchases between deal announcement and close, building cash and positioning Devon to resume buybacks immediately post-close at levels above legacy activity.

Devon has initiated a complete portfolio review of all combined assets against strategic and financial criteria including capital efficiency, inventory depth, free cash flow, and overall fit, with combined full-year guidance to be provided in mid-June.

Devon has over 850 wells on fully autonomous AI-driven artificial lift optimization (Smart gas lift), with pilot uplift of 2%–3% and full implementation results exceeding pilot levels, targeting rollout to 1,500 wells across the portfolio.

Strategic portfolio actions over the past year have delivered over $1 billion in present value uplift, including the upcoming Fervo IPO (Devon led the Series D round), which provides a public marker for the investment's value.

Devon's Waha exposure will decline to approximately 10%–15% once the Blackcomb pipeline comes online later this year, and Q1 included shut-ins of high-GOR wells to manage gas price exposure; Q1 acquisition capital of roughly $150 million was 90% Delaware Basin, adding well over 100 net locations from the ground game since last year.
Kaiser Aluminum delivered record adjusted EBITDA of $310 million in 2025, up approximately $69 million (more than 25% growth) from 2024.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 21.3%, approximately 470 basis points above the 2024 margin of 16.6%, with second half margins improving to nearly 24%.

Free cash flow for 2026 is anticipated to be in the range of $120 million to $140 million, with capital expenditures expected between $120 million and $130 million.
Net debt leverage ratio improved to 3.4x at December 31, 2025, down from 4.3x at December 31, 2024.

Aerospace and high-strength shipments are expected to increase 10% to 15% in 2026, with conversion revenue up approximately 5% to 10%, as commercial aerospace OEM destocking is expected to largely dissipate by year-end.

Packaging conversion revenue is expected to grow 15% to 20% in 2026 on shipment growth of 5% to 10%, driven by the shift toward higher-margin coated products now at approximately 75% of mix and growing.
The company completed a $500 million offering of senior notes due in 2034, with fixed annual interest costs of $54 million, extending its long-term debt maturity profile.

Rising metal prices drove $168 million of working capital usage in 2025, and the 2026 outlook assumes no continued metal price tailwind, meaning any further metal price gains would represent upside to guidance.

Kaiser is investing in incremental automotive capacity for specialty ICE truck and SUV products where it holds close to 100% supply position, adding approximately $10-12 million to expected CapEx, with capacity expected to come online within 12 to 18 months.
Q1 2026 revenue grew 25.7% year-over-year to $199.4 million, exceeding expectations on both the top and bottom line.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q1 was $14.1 million or 7.1% of revenue, an 880 basis point year-over-year improvement and well above prior guidance of 3% to 4%.

Full-year 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $875 million-$885 million (17%-18% growth), and adjusted EBITDA margin guidance was raised to 12%-13%, with Q2 revenue guided to $218 million-$220 million.
Q1 gross margin reached 70.9%, up 210 basis points year-over-year, driven by manufacturing automation, workflow optimization, and scale benefits.
New stores (open less than 12 months) accounted for approximately 64% of year-over-year volume growth, while home enrollment held steady at ~23% of U.S. Zio Services volume.
The next-generation MCT release timeline was reaffirmed for first half 2027, with the FDA preferring a complete submission package later this year rather than rolling data.

A separately filed next-generation AI algorithm, expected to receive FDA approval later in 2026, could cut clinical technician review time by nearly half and is estimated to deliver well north of $100 million in cumulative value over five years.
An independent third-party review of iRhythm's quality management system was completed in Q1 with no material observations identified, supporting progress on the FDA warning letter remediation.

Management estimates the U.S. cardiac monitoring market at 6.5-7 million tests annually, including ~3.5 million long-term monitoring tests (with iRhythm holding ~72% share) and ~1 million MCT tests, against a 27 million at-risk patient TAM.

EHR-integrated accounts now represent approximately 53% of volume with more than 3/4 of the top 100 customers integrated, and primary care contributes over 30% of volume from more than 40,000 prescribers.

The Andersons reported record Q1 2026 net income of $33 million ($0.97 diluted EPS) and adjusted net income of $38 million ($1.12 per diluted share), versus adjusted net income of just $4 million ($0.12 per share) in Q1 2025.
Adjusted EBITDA grew to $91 million from $57 million in Q1 2025, with adjusted pretax earnings rising to $44 million from $3 million year-over-year.

Renewables segment pretax income jumped to $40 million from $15 million a year ago, including $26 million of 45Z producer tax credits recognized in the quarter, with EBITDA of $54 million versus $37 million.

Agribusiness adjusted pretax income improved to $18 million from breakeven in Q1 2025, with segment EBITDA rising to $49 million from $31 million on improved fertilizer margins and merchandising volatility.
Management reaffirmed its long-range EPS target of $7 per share by the end of 2028 and expects full-year 2026 adjusted tax rate of 14% to 18%, with Q1 booked at 14%.

Full-year 2026 capital spending is expected to be approximately $225 million excluding acquisitions, with Q1 capex of $52 million; long-term debt-to-EBITDA stands at 1.6x versus a stated target of below 2.5x.

Q1 ethanol margins were partially capped by hedges placed at historically favorable levels, but management noted no hedges are in place beyond Q1 and board crush currently looks favorable for Q2 and Q3.

Ethanol was trading as much as $1.30-$1.35/gallon under ARBOB recently (now ~$1.25), supporting blending economics with crude near $100/barrel and U.S. gasoline above $4.45/gallon, driving strong domestic and export demand.

The Port of Houston soybean meal export facility is on track for full operations in Q3 2026, the Carlsbad mineral plant is now operational, and the Clymers, Indiana ethanol debottlenecking project is expected to be completed by late 2027.

Management believes the grain cycle trough occurred in 2025 and expects a year-over-year shift from corn to soybeans for 2026 plantings, with corn acres still projected above the 5-year average and ~85% of producers having locked in fertilizer prices before the Iran conflict began.
